caa7_association_analysis: Two-sample t-test (adjusted for sex, age, TIV); Pearson's correlation coefficient; permutation testing; multilinear models; false discovery rate (FDR) correction; dominance analysis.
caa8_key_findings_brief: The study identified two reproducible OCD subtypes with contrasting gray matter morphological abnormalities and divergent disease epicenters, which also showed distinct associations with neurotransmitter receptors/transporters.
caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study identified two distinct and reproducible OCD subtypes. Subtype 1 showed significantly increased gray matter volume (GMV) in regions including the frontal gyrus, precuneus, insula, hippocampus, parahippocampal gyrus, amygdala, and temporal gyrus, while subtype 2 exhibited significantly decreased GMV in the frontal gyrus, precuneus, insula, superior parietal gyrus, temporal gyrus, and fusiform gyrus (FDR corrected p < 0.05 for both). Subtype 1 had a higher proportion of male patients (p < 0.001). The subtypes exhibited divergent disease epicenters, with Subtype 1 in the middle frontal gyrus and Subtype 2 in the striatum, thalamus, and hippocampus (permutation p < 0.01 for both). Distinct associations with neurotransmitter receptors/transporters were found, with 5HT1A linked to Subtype 1 and 5HT2A to Subtype 2, based on multilinear models (adjusted R²=0.43 for Subtype 1, R²=0.34 for Subtype 2; FDR-corrected p < 0.001).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional sample; limited clinical information; individual variations in neurotransmitter systems (based on public datasets); lower educational levels in OCD patients.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, it was conducted using a cross-sectional sample, raising questions about the stability and generalizability of the identified subtypes. Second, the limited clinical information available restricted our ability to explore potential differences in other clinical aspects between the subtypes. Third, individual variations in neurotransmitter systems may affect the observed associations between structural abnormalities and neurotransmitter systems, which were based on publicly available datasets [103]. Finally, patients with OCD in our study had lower educational levels compared to healthy controls.

caa11_application_notes: Identification of two robust OCD subtypes using k-means clustering on Z-scores derived from normative models of gray matter volume. Reproducibility analysis included subsampling, an alternative brain atlas (AAL), and different distance metrics. Disease epicenter mapping was informed by a structural covariance network, and dominance analysis was used to identify key neurotransmitter receptors associated with each subtype.
gn1_general_note: The study focused on first-episode, untreated OCD patients. Additional software tools used include SPM12 for group-level differences in GMV and a Python toolbox (https://github.com/kaladharprajapati/dominance_analysis) for dominance analysis.
